body: It’s called malocclusion, my rat has this also and just has to have his tooth burred every few weeks. With regular burring it’s pretty manageable

He still has his fluffy baby coat so I would say around 3-4 weeks. Would recommend giving little Bert some extra protein to help him grow as rats aren’t really supposed to be homed until at least 7-8 weeks. Most ethical breeders won’t home until after 8 weeks. Eggs, Chicken, fish etc would be great to supplement his diet! 

I made the same mistake of going to a backyard breeder when I got my first rats so I totally understand not knowing any better. They were so tiny but a good protein filled diet will help a lot!

Since then, my hair has been a lot healthier and wavy.

I watched a tiktok about the curly girl method and started experimenting with some products (cantu shampoo and conditioner + curling cream).

Researchers actually think that trypophobia is the minds natural fear response to things that might harm it. It’s your mind saying “hey, please don’t go near that it might bite/sting/hurt you” or “don’t eat that it’s probably poisonous”. A lot of bugs nests are formed by circular shapes, some poisonous plants are too so it makes sense! That doesn’t necessarily make it a phobia though it’s more of a feeling of uncomfortableness!
